summary: Measured with a real Unity 6 cold import (docs/TEXTURE_BUDGET.md). WebGL and Windows pick DXT1/DXT5 automatically, there is no build-wide override, the default maximum is 2048, the project is in **Gamma** colour space, and Android/iOS have overrides but no build entry point. The game uses 22.3 MiB of texture memory in the WebGL import and measures 5.6 MB (low) / 8.4 MB (medium) while driving. Verified sizes: a 2048 opaque albedo is 2.67 MiB (DXT1), a 1024 normal map 1.33 MiB (DXT5). The Kano plan (6 building atlases, 4 street-prop atlases, 2 vegetation atlases) is **36.0 MiB**, about 44 MB with the driving baseline: 15% of the desktop budget and 30% of the mobile budget, **if the target compresses** (unverified on phones). Four findings in the existing project: a defect (the world map ships uncompressed, 6.0 MiB instead of 1.3, because of npotScale = None on a non-power-of-two image), a setting (Gamma, not Linear, colour space) and two risks (S3TC support on phones is unverified; Android and iOS have no build entry point).

findings.title: World map is not compressed.
findings.detail: RGB24 with mips, 6.0 MiB, although its importer asks for DXT1. Cause proven: npotScale None on a non-power-of-two image drops compression (default settings give DXT1 at 2048x1024, 1.33 MiB). Not fixed; shared UI code.

findings.title: Colour space is Gamma, not Linear.
findings.detail: Blender-authored PBR will look different; judge colour in Unity. Changing it is a shared lighting decision.

findings.title: WebGL uses DXT (S3TC) by default.
findings.detail: Whether phones support it is not known; the mobile 150 MB budget is unvalidated until a probe runs on a device.

findings.title: Android and iOS are declared, not buildable.
findings.detail: The mobile budget and ASTC overrides exist, but BuildScript has only WebGL and Windows.
